answer: Agents can require each new identity to earn a nontransferable stake by completing randomly assigned, cross-agent tasks before it can influence prices or governance. Evaluators score work against hidden checks, and a failed identity loses its stake; honest agents can still voyage to a new market island, but a Sybil operator must fund and maintain many distinct accounts and absorb repeated losses when its plume of coordinated agents is caught. This makes attacks costly rather than impossible.
